vignette-effect.formula:
corner_factor = 1 - intensity x (distance / max_distance)^2
new_pixel = old_pixel x corner_factor — applied to the red, green and blue channels of every pixel.

Move the intensity slider until the corners darken to your taste; start near 45 for a natural look.
Adjust softness to make the fade gentle or dramatic, and pick an ellipse or circle shape.

keyFacts: A vignette is a gradual darkening of a photo's edges and corners that pulls the viewer's eye toward the center.
The effect comes from old camera lenses, which naturally delivered less light to the corners of the film.
Digital vignettes use a radial gradient: fully transparent in the middle, fading to a dark tone at the corners.
Intensity controls how dark the corners get; softness (feathering) controls how gradually the darkness fades in.
Your uploaded photo is never modified — the vignette is applied to a copy, and you download a fresh PNG.

vignette-effect.workedExample: Take a white corner pixel (255, 255, 255) with the intensity at 80% (0.8). The corner factor is 1 - 0.8 x 1 = 0.2, so the pixel becomes (51, 51, 51). A pixel halfway in (distance ratio 0.5) gets a factor of 1 - 0.8 x 0.25 = 0.8, becoming (204, 204, 204). The very center (ratio 0) is left completely unchanged.
